newsitem.title: USA: Deere says earnings jump 24 pct for quarter.
newsitem.headline: Deere says earnings jump 24 pct for quarter.

text.p: Deere & Co. said Tuesday its earnings jumped 24 percent in the latest quarter, thanks to a growing global economy, which is boosting demand for agriculture and construction equipment.
The company said it earned $252.7 million, or $1.00 per share, in its fiscal third quarter ended July 31, vs. year-earlier earnings of $204.4 million, or 79 cents a share.
Sales rose 18 percent to $3.43 billion from $2.90 billion a year earlier.
"The higher profits resulted from strong worldwide retail demand for the company's products, especially tractors and combines," said Chairman and CEO Hans W. Becherer.
"Retail demand for 1997 is benefiting from a growing global economy, healthy agricultural markets and generally high levels of farmer confidence," he said.

Becherer said that demand for construction equipment is strong and the company expects sales to remain at current levels throughout the rest of the year as economic growth, rising income and low inflation boosts the housing market.
Deere's stock was unchanged at $56.94 in early morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
